lines.line: It points north. What use is that to the gate or the garrison, stranger?
Three times is hard to blame on a twitchy hand. Could it help the patrols in fog, Captain?

turns.said: It always points north, even at night or in fog.

lines.line: Then we test it against a known bearing in the fog. If it holds, the patrols may have use for it.
A fair test, Captain. Stranger, can you show it holds when the fog comes down?

turns.said: Your men could find their way with it on patrol.

lines.line: That is what we are testing, stranger. When the fog comes, you will show it against a known bearing; until then, it proves nothing.
Fair enough, but a straight north reading won't tell us how it fares on the moor. We wait for fog, then put it to the test.

turns.said: Good evening! Is this your inn?

lines.line: Oh, love, it is. Come in out of the road—are you looking for a bed, or just a bite to eat?

turns.line: Oh, love, it is. Come in out of the road—are you looking for a bed, or just a bite to eat?

turns.said: I'm looking for somewhere to sleep tonight.

lines.line: A bed, then, love. I’ve room tonight; come inside and we’ll settle what it costs before you turn in.

turns.line: A bed, then, love. I’ve room tonight; come inside and we’ll settle what it costs before you turn in.

turns.said: And who's this? A friend of yours?

lines.line: That’s Bren, my brother. He’s keeping an eye on the road, love—no need to look so wary of him.
